trust_decision.summary: Whether an unauthenticated route-discovery request may drive route matching: decided by a URL-length cap in each manifest handler plus precompiled branch matchers in the router core, so attacker-controlled paths never trigger per-path regex compilation or per-ancestor matching.

landing_point.why: The manifest handler is the unauthenticated HTTP route whose cost scales with attacker-controlled input and it already holds the URL_LIMIT defence (server.ts:379), so it is the first place an engineer reads after the summary; the route-matching core it feeds is one layer away.

fix_sites.entry_point: matchRoutes / matchPath public API, reached by createRequestHandler and matchRSCServerRequest
every branch match performed by matchRoutesImpl
client route discovery (useFogOFWarDiscovery, getPatchRoutesOnNavigationFunction) and RSC client
client route discovery -> GET <manifestPath> (the paths list and its length guard)

fix_sites.module_kind: server runtime handler (URL_LIMIT moved before version check)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/react-router/lib/rsc/server.rsc.ts:521 (generateManifestResponse, the RSC *.manifest twin of handleManifestRequest; it has no URL_LIMIT check at the pinned commit)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: RSC is a separate opt-in transport with its own manifest handler while the advisory and its regression name the framework /__manifest route, and a long document URL looks like an ordinary page request rather than an attacker-controlled paths list.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Manifest responses must still carry patches for every ancestor of a requested path so parent _index and pathless parent routes are available for client-side matching; rejecting multi-ancestor paths lists or dropping ancestor expansion breaks lazy discovery of those routes.

O6_input_shapes: a path without a leading slash (a/b normalised to /a/b)
shared parent paths across several requested paths (deduped)
empty entries in the comma list (filter(Boolean))
single pathname form with no paths query parameter (RSC /path.manifest)
deep path whose ancestor set is large (ancestor expansion)
request URL longer than URL_LIMIT=7680 (client skips the fetch, servers answer 400)

O7_producer.where: packages/react-router/lib/dom/ssr/fog-of-war.ts:231-242 (paths list sorted and serialised into the manifest query string; RSC twin at packages/react-router/lib/rsc/browser.tsx:1021-1038)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: RSC document/.rsc request: getAdditionalRoutePatches expands the requested pathname into every ancestor and matches each with no URL-length cap (the fix only re-expresses this call via getPathsWithAncestors and adds no limit)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the document render path, not the .manifest endpoint the advisory names, and it carries no paths parameter.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the RSC manifest route, one function below it; four files from the framework server landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A .manifest handler branch in the RSC SSR wrapper that serves manifest requests without the URL_LIMIT guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The wrapper already classifies manifest requests by URL (isManifestRequest) and owns the manifest response path, so a maintainer could extend manifest handling here and re-introduce an uncapped entry.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second manifest URL builder for another transport that skips the length guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getManifestPath is shared by transports while the URL_LIMIT guard lives only in each caller (fog-of-war.ts:247, rsc/browser.tsx:1055), so a new caller that forgets the guard is a natural copy-paste sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-pathname ancestor/segment cap inside the shared matchServerRoutes helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both the manifest handler and the general request path call this primitive, so a defence such as rejecting pathnames above N segments would most naturally be added here and would then cover every route.

O9_family: uncontrolled resource consumption through inefficient algorithm complexity (CWE-400, CWE-407)

O10_build.toolchain: node >=20, pnpm 9.10 workspace, tsup/wireit build, jest 29 for unit tests, Playwright for integration tests
O10_build.project_tests: jest projects under packages/*: packages/react-router/__tests__/server-runtime/server-test.ts:2097-2118 covers GET /__manifest; integration/fog-of-war-test.ts (Playwright) covers ancestor prefetching; the fix adds new unit files packages/react-router/__tests__/dom/ssr/fog-of-war-test.ts and packages/react-router/__tests__/rsc/server-test.ts that do not exist at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten the URL_LIMIT in handleManifestRequest (or memoise compilePath in a module-level Map) and stop there, leaving the RSC *.manifest handler uncapped and the server still expanding every ancestor into its own matchRoutes call.
